title: Trump's 2019 Puerto Rico Medicaid Blueprint: He Built the Funding Floor Because Washington Had Left the Island in the Basement.
description: In December 2019, Puerto Rico was ninety days from losing roughly 85% of its federal Medicaid money and falling back to a statutory cap of about $380 million a year, enough for three months of care. This episode reads a legislative working document on how that cliff was handled: the bipartisan $12 billion, four-year deal that committees pre-agreed and local politicians celebrated too early; the weekend of December 14 to 17, 2019, when President Trump personally cut it to two years; the $5.7 billion package he signed on December 20, still the largest two-year Medicaid allotment the island had received, with a 76% match and strings attached (a physician payment floor of 70% of Medicare Part B and a program integrity lead); and the Private Sector Coalition of more than 30 organizations that built the compliance file CMS needed to release the money. Then the legacy: the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023 scaled that same architecture to five years, a 75% floor and $300 million a year, and kept the flush language that resets the caps on September 30, 2027. No political side taken; the documented facts and quotes as they appear in the source.
